description:
Prepyr is an AI-assisted browser workspace for people who work with business data and want a more approachable way to understand it. Users upload a CSV or single-sheet Excel file, inspect data quality, review supported cleaning transformations, ask analytical questions in plain language, create charts, and build editable reports. Single-sheet Excel files are converted into a CSV workspace.

Prepyr supports exploration, cleanup, answering business questions, investigating changes, creating charts, and reporting. Tasks may be one-off, exploratory or repeated; owning a recurring report is not a requirement. Review points, version history, reusable transformations and supporting evidence let users inspect changes and calculations on one prepared table.

The product is self-service and credit-based. Team, API, integration, shared-workspace, SLA, white-label, automatic multi-file joining and complex multi-sheet workbook preservation are not included in currently purchasable plans.
remarks:
Prioritize nontechnical or lightly technical business users at startups, and include equally relevant professionals at other growing businesses who regularly work with data, including employees and founders in operations, finance, marketing, sales and customer success. Do not limit the audience to technology startups, small companies, owners, agencies or recurring-report authors. Consider both technology and nontechnology startups, including startups that serve consumers; their employees are professional prospects, not private consumers.

For each prospect provide the organization, named professional or relevant role, evidenced responsibilities or business activity, why a supported Prepyr capability could help, and direct public source URLs. Include cadence and pain only when actually evidenced; neither is mandatory. Do not infer low technical proficiency, spreadsheet problems, purchasing authority, budget, file compatibility or buying intent. Keep these unknown or conditional.

Offer every initial prospect a free guided first analysis of one CSV or single-sheet Excel dataset, using supported Prepyr features to explore questions and create charts or findings. Scope is one dataset after agreement; no custom integrations, unlimited free service, free credits of an unspecified amount, automatic subscription or guaranteed outcomes. Data sharing is optional and must be authorized by the recipient.

Allow professional work-email enrichment: require independent per-address verification, current-company matching and separate provider-evidence labeling. Reject personal addresses and unverified or catch-all results. Public email publication is optional for these verified contacts.

Startup status is a preference, not a mandatory qualification or an age/headcount rule. Do not reject an otherwise relevant professional at a growing business because current startup status or venture funding is unknown. Ground the actual professional responsibility and useful product fit; keep internal workflow and technical proficiency conditional.
customerDescription:
Nontechnical and lightly technical professionals at startups and other growing businesses who regularly work with business data. Include operations, finance, marketing, sales, customer success and business generalists, as well as founders. Search across technology and nontechnology startups and across companies serving businesses or consumers. Prefer startups without excluding equally relevant professionals at other growing businesses; no fixed headcount, industry, seniority or founder-only restriction.

Relevant tasks include understanding sales or customer activity, reviewing campaign results, investigating operational changes, cleaning a dataset, answering a business question, exploring survey results, preparing charts, and making business decisions. Recurring reports are one possible use, not the required use.

Find public evidence of responsibilities and data-related activity that could benefit from approachable analysis, cleanup or visualization. A role title alone is a lead to investigate, not proof of pain or proficiency. A person does not need to publicly advertise a spreadsheet problem or a fixed reporting cadence. File compatibility and willingness to use a self-service product can be confirmed in conversation.

Prioritize likely actual users over consulting firms selling reporting services. Do not automatically select agencies or analytics vendors merely because their service pages mention reports. Exclude private consumers and referral-only prospects. Reject essential incompatible requirements only when they are evidenced.
customerComments:
Search for relevant people and their responsibilities using LinkedIn public professional profiles plus official company websites and other public business sources. Rotate across operations, finance, marketing, sales, customer success and founder/generalist roles, and across technology and nontechnology startups. Do not impose a small-company cap, founder/owner requirement, B2B-only customer-market restriction, recurring report, reporting cadence, exact file type or documented pain as a universal gate.

Qualification needs verified identity/current company, requested geography, an evidenced relevant responsibility or data-related activity, a supported product capability and an appropriate publicly sourced business email or independently provider-verified professional work email matching the person and current company. Separate professional role evidence from company-level evidence. Do not transfer a former employer's activities to the current employer. Technical proficiency, purchasing authority, budget, buying intent and internal systems stay unknown unless evidenced.

Rank by person-level relevance and product usefulness. Keep discovery broad, then research and qualify. Existing reporting services or a generic job title alone do not establish fit. Offer the authorized free first-dataset session in every initial email without inventing pain or additional commercial terms.

Startup status is a preference, not an exclusion gate. Equally relevant professionals at other growing businesses qualify. Missing startup classification alone is never a rejection reason.
